quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 7 (JA)/TD03793_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I 'GREL PA (Abhisamayālaṃkāra Nāma Prajñā Pāramita Upadeśa Śāstra Vṛtti)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Haribhadra, འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། (Tengyur, Tōh. 3793), gloss on the ten instructions
quotes.why: Haribhadra's own gloss on མ་ཞེན, which the paragraph quotes as its ཚིག་དོན — note that the Tengyur text reads བསོད་ནམས where the yig cha reads བསོད་ཉམས.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 7 (JA)/TD03793_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I MAN NGAG GI BSTAN BCOS MNGON PAR RTOGS PA'I RGYAN ZHES BYA BA'I 'GREL PA (Abhisamayālaṃkāra Nāma Prajñā Pāramita Upadeśa Śāstra Vṛtti)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Haribhadra, འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། (Tengyur, Tōh. 3793), same list, the gloss on ལམ་ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་པ
quotes.why: Haribhadra's gloss on the third instruction, quoted in the paragraph; the whole psychology of discouragement the yig cha elaborates is already here in one clause.
The root line of the Ornament whose two words མ་ཞེན and ཡོངས་སུ་མི་ངལ་ are the lemmata of the first two-thirds of this paragraph; ལམ་ནི་ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་པ follows on the next line.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 3 (GA)/TD03790-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA (Pañca Viṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཉི་ཤུ་ལྔ་པ། the eight-chapter recension in the Tengyur (Tōh. 3790), vol. GA
quotes.why: The Ornament-ordered recension of the 25,000 closes the མ་ཞེན sūtra section at exactly the sentence the paragraph quotes as its hinge, and labels it; the yig cha's sūtra boundaries are this recension's.

quotes.file: Tengyur/03 SHES PHYIN_Perfection of Wisdom (Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 3 (GA)/TD03790-1_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA (Pañca Viṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཉི་ཤུ་ལྔ་པ། the eight-chapter recension in the Tengyur (Tōh. 3790), vol. GA
quotes.why: The same recension ends the ལམ་ཡོངས་སུ་འཛིན་པ sūtra section with the very sentence the paragraph gives as its closing 'up to' point, and names the instruction.

quotes.file: Kangyur/3. NYI KHRI (Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā)/VOL 1 (KA)/KL00009E1INC_SHES RAB KYI PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA STONG PHRAG NYI SHU LNGA PA 1_The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 Lines, Part 1 (Pañca Viṃśati Sāhasrikā Prajñā Pāramitā 1)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: The closing sentence of the ཡོངས་སུ་མི་ངལ sūtra passage in the Kangyur translation: it reads སྨད་པར་འགྱུར་བ, 'despised', where the yig cha's quotation reads པདྨར་འགྱུར་བ.

quotes.file: Tengyur/04 DBU MA_Middle Way School (Madhyamaka)/VOL 10 (LA)/TD03871_BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA'I SPYOD PA LA 'JUG PA (Bodhisattva Caryāvatāra)_unicode.txt
quotes.why: Śāntideva's list of the three kinds of laziness, which the yig cha borrows (via Tsongkhapa) to map the three instructions; the very next line ties the first kind to relishing the pleasure of idleness.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་སྤྱི་དོན། the outline of the ten instructions, earlier in this same text
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen's own outline of this section, in this text: here the laziness countered by མ་ཞེན is སྙོམས་ལས་འཛིན་པ, where p402–p403 call it ངན་ཞེན.
Tsongkhapa's reading of Haribhadra's clause with བསོད་ཉམས glossed as 'the arising of pleasure' — the source of the paragraph's བསོད་ཉམས་དེ་བདེ་བ་སྐྱེ་བ.
Tsongkhapa explaining why non-conceit cures weariness: the discouraged practitioner's weariness rests on conceit about the long practice already done.
The direct speech the paragraph puts in the discouraged bodhisattva's mouth — 'I cannot do such a thing' — is Tsongkhapa's, not Haribhadra's.
Gyaltsab Je's thesis for མ་ཞེན — non-attachment to bad activities of the three doors — which is the paragraph's own thesis wording; but he takes a different sūtra sentence as its instance.
Gyaltsab Je keeps Haribhadra's བསོད་ནམས and makes it the merit of body etc. attached to ordinary activity — a different reading of the word the paragraph glosses as pleasure.

quotes.citation: ལེགས་བཤད་གསེར་ཕྲེང་། སྐབས་དང་པོ། the later summary of the ten instructions
quotes.why: Tsongkhapa himself, in a later summary, calls the first laziness ངན་ཞེན rather than སྙོམས་ལས — so the double labelling in this yig cha goes back to the gser phreng.
Ārya Vimuktisena, reading the same sūtra passage: he too has སྨད་པར་འགྱུར་བའི་ལུས, and he states the link the paragraph relies on — conceit is what brings weariness.
